newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weak as oversupply dominates.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weak as oversupply dominates.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures shed afternoon gains to close weaker on Wednesday as bearish spot market fundamentals overwhelmed supportive news of a fall in U.S. gasoline stocks, dealers said.
"There is genuine oversupply at the moment. Margins are good but there's only so much crude you can run and the contango isn't deep enough to start filling storage," said a trader.
May Brent crude closed down 26 cents at $19.28 a barrel, more than 60 cents off the session high of $19.90 posted in the wake of news of a 900,000-barrel fall in U.S. gasoline stocks last week.
"Once we dipped back through the break levels the market returned to well-trodden areas and it didn't take much to get to the bottom of the range," said a broker.
May Brent found support at $19.24 a barrel, brokers said.
Spot North Sea crude cargoes continued to trade at big discounts to forward paper values on Wednesday amid ample supply and thinner demand due to scheduled spring refinery maintenance programmes.
Earlier, U.S. data showing gasoline stocks were still lagging year-ago levels by eight million barrels with the driving season fast approaching helped lift the energy complex.
But the EIA reported a smaller fall in crude stocks than the American Petroleum Insitute (API) on Tuesday, and that also helped dent confidence.
IPE gas oil closed virtually unchanged, the prompt April gas oil lagging Brent's afternoon gains to close up just 25 cents at $172.50 a tonne.
